header_evidence.locator: SS1-SRC-de2cdd0b85f6: first paragraph of word/document.xml (the first body element); the next paragraph is the 'WEEK / TOPIC' scheme table heading
header_evidence.explanation: The opening heading is a generic scheme title; it does not name the subject, the class or '1st Term' (it reads 'ALPHA TERM'; the term comes from the archive folder '1st Term SS1_'). The document has no 'SUBJECT:' or 'CLASS:' line. The subject is therefore confirmed from teaching content only: the scheme's Week 1 topic reads 'Introduction to food and nutrition', the lesson body opens with 'WEEK 1 / INTRODUCTION TO FOOD AND NUTRITION', and the scheme covers nutrients, vitamins, mineral salts, deficiency symptoms and the digestive system. It is not Catering Craft; 'Hotel and catering management' appears only as one item in a Week 2 careers list. The filename 'F _ N.docx' was not used as evidence. Heading occurs once in text extracted directly from the original DOCX XML; uniqueness was not checked on importer/mammoth output (importer run deferred).

header_evidence.locator: SS1-SRC-0579303326ae: second non-empty paragraph of mammoth.extractRawText output (the importer's own .docx call; character offset 18), directly after the first paragraph 'SIGMA TERM (2nd)' (offset 0) and before 'SSS 1' and 'SCHEME OF WORK FOR SIGMA TERM'; the paragraph is 'FOOD AND NUTRITION' with no surrounding spaces
header_evidence.explanation: The heading 'FOOD AND NUTRITION' occurs once in the extracted text (case-insensitive search also finds one occurrence). It names Food and Nutrition, not Catering Craft; the document has no SUBJECT or CLASS label and no catering wording. It equals the canonical subject 'Food and Nutrition' apart from case, so no source_alias rule is declared. The filename 'F _ N.docx' was not used as evidence. The scheme agrees: revision of the scientific study of foods, measurement, effects of heat on food, food tests, the food composition table, meal planning, reproductive health and malnutrition. The document's own term label is 'SIGMA TERM (2nd)', which matches the manifest 2nd Term folder. Only the header and opening scheme were inspected; no week inventory is recorded here.

coverage.objective: The opening statements of Week 1: the search for food has been the occupation of mankind from the onset and food is very important to day to day life (line 111).

coverage.objective: The definitions of food and of nutrients: food as what nourishes the body, any substance which after consumption, digestion and absorption produces energy, promotes growth, repairs body tissues and regulates all body processes (line 113), and nutrients as the chemicals in food that let it do so (line 115).

evidence.explanation: Definition of food with four stated functions (energy, growth, repair of tissues, regulation of body processes).
Definition of nutrients as 'the chemicals present in it'. The source does not name any nutrient or class of nutrient in Week 1.

coverage.objective: The definition of nutrition: the study of the various nutrients in relation to their effect on the human body, and the statement that nutrition is the science of food in relation to health (line 117).

Point 1 (Food is important to man) restates line 111 and points 3, 7 and 8 are generic; the six factors (availability of food, income, food in season, ignorance, storage/preservation, facilities available) have no explanation or example, and the introduction says the factors include these, so the list is open-ended. Any explanation a lesson adds is new content, not source content.
open_items.required_action: Author explanations only as visibly original teaching with truthful provenance, flag every added claim for FN-FACT-T1-NUTRITION-CLAIMS, and do not present the list as exhaustive.

open_items.detail: Week 1 makes health claims without a source: a strong correlation between good food and intellectual development (line 123), well fed people having more resistance to diseases than the poorly nourished (line 129), and the proportion of food consumed having a positive or negative effect on the body (line 133), alongside the four functions of food at line 113. The existing item FN-FACT-T1-NUTRITION-CLAIMS lists claims from later weeks only and does not depend on FN-WK-T1-W01. No dose, treatment or classroom observation occurs anywhere in the Week 1 body (scanned).
open_items.required_action: Verify or flag lines 113, 123, 129 and 133 through FN-FACT-T1-NUTRITION-CLAIMS before a lesson adopts them, keeping the source wording separate from any correction; add no dose, treatment or practical observation.
